title: Parent Study & Practice Guide
subtitle: Subject-wise help for parents to prepare kids for Joy of Learning - I

subjects.subject: Hindi
parentTips: Practice 15-20 minutes daily — short sessions work best for Class 1.
Read each word aloud together, then let your child read it alone.
Give a small dictation (5 words) every day from the practice lists.
Ask your child to recite the poem नया सवेरा with actions — it helps memory.

topics.name: मात्रा ज्ञान (Matras)
topics.whatToKnow: Child should identify and use vowel signs: ा (आ), ि (इ), ी (ई), ु (उ), ू (ऊ) in words. Example: क + ा = का, क + ि = कि.
topics.practiceAtHome: Write 10 simple words (नाम, दिन, नानी, गुड़िया, फूल) and ask your child to circle the matra and say which vowel sound it makes.

topics.name: बारहखड़ी (Barahkhadi)
topics.whatToKnow: The 12 forms of each consonant: क का कि की कु कू के कै को कौ कं कः. Child should say and write the barahkhadi of at least क, ख, ग, म, न.
topics.practiceAtHome: Make it a chant! Sing the barahkhadi of one letter each day while clapping. Then ask your child to write it from memory.

topics.name: संयुक्ताक्षर और संयुक्त व्यंजन (Joint letters)
topics.whatToKnow: Two consonants joined together, e.g. क्ष, त्र, ज्ञ, श्र and words like बच्चा, सच्चा, पत्ता.
topics.practiceAtHome: Point at joint letters in a Hindi storybook or newspaper heading and ask your child to spot the two letters hiding inside.

topics.name: र के रूप (Forms of Ra)
topics.whatToKnow: र changes shape when joined: र् + क = र्क (रेफ on top, e.g. सूर्य), क + र = क्र (below, e.g. क्रम).
topics.practiceAtHome: Write सूर्य, धर्म, क्रम, ट्रक on paper and ask your child to find where the र is hiding in each word.

topics.name: पाठ 1 - नया सवेरा (कविता)
topics.whatToKnow: Child should recite the poem with correct pronunciation and know the meaning of simple words in it.
topics.practiceAtHome: Recite one stanza at a time. Record your child on your phone and play it back — kids love it and self-correct!

topics.name: पाठ 2 - शीशा
topics.whatToKnow: Child should read the lesson fluently and answer simple questions about the story.
topics.practiceAtHome: After reading, ask: कहानी में कौन था? क्या हुआ? Let your child answer in Hindi in full sentences.

quiz.q: म की बारहखड़ी के पहले 4 रूप बोलो।
'बच्चा' में संयुक्त अक्षर कौन सा है?

quiz.a: र्य में — रेफ (र्) ऊपर लगा है

subjects.subject: Environmental Science
parentTips: EVS is all around you — revise while walking, cooking, or driving!
Ask 'why' and 'where' questions in daily life to connect chapters to real things.
Use family photos to revise the Different Families chapter.
Do a house tour and name every room and its use for Sweet Home chapter.

topics.name: Chapter 1: Knowing Myself
topics.whatToKnow: My name, age, birthday, body parts and their uses, sense organs, things I like, what makes me special.
topics.practiceAtHome: Play 'Simon Says' with body parts. Ask: Which body part helps you see? Hear? Smell? Walk? Hold things?

topics.name: Chapter 2: Different Families
topics.whatToKnow: Small family (parents + children), big/joint family (with grandparents, uncles, aunts), family members' names and relations, how families care for each other.
topics.practiceAtHome: Open the family album and ask your child to point out and name relations: dadaji, dadiji, chacha, bua, mama, mausi. Ask: Is our family small or big?

topics.name: Chapter 3: Sweet Home
topics.whatToKnow: Rooms in a house (bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, living room) and their uses. Types of houses — kutcha and pucca house, and why we need a house.
topics.practiceAtHome: Do a 2-minute house tour: 'Which room do we cook in? Sleep in? Bathe in?' Draw a house together and label the rooms.

topics.name: Chapter 4: Our Neighbourhood
topics.whatToKnow: Places around us — school, park, hospital, post office, market, bank, police station — and what each place is for. Community helpers we see there.
topics.practiceAtHome: On your next drive/walk, play 'spot the place': every time you pass a shop, hospital or park, ask what people do there.

quiz.q: Which sense organ helps us smell?
What do we call a family with grandparents, uncles and aunts living together?
In which room do we cook food?
Which house is strong, made of bricks and cement?
Where do we go when we are sick?

subjects.subject: Computer Science
parentTips: Show the real devices at home — pointing at an actual keyboard beats any book!
Keep it playful: 'input' is what we GIVE the computer, 'output' is what it GIVES BACK.
Revise using your own laptop/phone: name each part together.
Draw the IPO cycle as three boxes with arrows — kids remember diagrams.

topics.name: Module 1: Types of Computers
topics.whatToKnow: Desktop (stays on a table), Laptop (can carry, folds), Tablet (touch screen), Smartphone (small computer in pocket). Where each one is used.
topics.practiceAtHome: Point at devices at home and ask: Is this a desktop, laptop, tablet or smartphone? Which one can we carry in a pocket?

topics.name: Module 1: IPO Cycle
topics.whatToKnow: IPO = Input → Process → Output. We give the computer instructions (Input), it thinks (Process), and shows the result (Output). Example: press 2 + 3 on calculator (input), it calculates (process), shows 5 (output).
topics.practiceAtHome: Use a calculator together. Say aloud: 'We typed — that's INPUT. It's thinking — PROCESS. It showed the answer — OUTPUT!'

topics.name: Module 2: Input Devices
topics.whatToKnow: Devices used to give data to the computer: Keyboard (typing), Mouse (clicking/pointing), Microphone (voice), Scanner (pictures into computer).
topics.practiceAtHome: Sit at your computer and let your child touch each input device and say its name and what it does.

topics.name: Module 2: Output Devices
topics.whatToKnow: Devices that show results: Monitor (shows pictures/videos), Printer (prints on paper), Speaker (gives sound).
topics.practiceAtHome: Play a song and ask: which device is giving us the sound? Print or show a picture and ask which device did that.

topics.name: Module 2: Storage Devices
topics.whatToKnow: Devices that store our data: Hard disk (inside computer), Pen drive/USB (small, portable), CD/DVD.
topics.practiceAtHome: Show a pen drive if you have one — 'this tiny box can carry your photos and songs!' Ask: where does the computer keep its memories?

quiz.q: Which computer can you fold and carry?
Which device do we use to type?
Is a printer an input or output device?
quiz.a: Output device — it gives results out on paper

quiz.q: Which device gives us sound from the computer?

subjects.subject: Mathematics
parentTips: Do 10 minutes of oral math daily — while eating or in the car.
Use real objects for addition and subtraction: toys, spoons, biscuits.
Practice writing numbers neatly — marks are lost on unreadable digits.
Focus extra on subtraction with borrowing-free problems first, then harder ones.

topics.name: Chapter 1: Numbers and Numeration
topics.whatToKnow: Count, read and write numbers up to 100. Number names, before/after/between, greater (>) and smaller (<), ascending & descending order, tens and ones (e.g. 47 = 4 tens + 7 ones).
topics.practiceAtHome: Ask: what comes after 39? Before 70? Between 55 and 57? Which is bigger — 63 or 36? Break numbers: '25 is how many tens and ones?'

topics.name: Chapter 2: Addition
topics.whatToKnow: Add numbers up to 20 (and 2-digit without carrying), addition on the number line, adding zero, word problems ('in all', 'altogether', 'total' mean ADD).
topics.practiceAtHome: Use toys: 'You have 7 cars, I give you 6 more — count the total!' Practice 5 sums daily. Draw jumps on a number line for 8 + 5.

topics.name: Chapter 3: Subtraction (till pg 53)
topics.whatToKnow: Take away/minus, subtraction on the number line, subtracting zero, subtracting the same number gives 0, word problems ('left', 'remaining' mean SUBTRACT).
topics.practiceAtHome: Use biscuits: '10 biscuits, you ate 4 — how many left?' Mix addition and subtraction so your child reads the sign carefully (+ or −).

quiz.q: Ria had 12 balloons. 5 flew away. How many are left?

subjects.subject: Kannada
parentTips: Read Kannada words aloud together daily — fluency comes from hearing + speaking.
Use flashcards (ಮಿಂಚು ಪಟ್ಟಿ) for ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರ words — the school also practices this way.
Practice writing numbers ೧-೯೦ a few rows each day, not all at once.
Recite the poem ಬಳ್ಳಿದ ಹಕ್ಕಿ with rhythm and claps.

topics.name: ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರಗಳು (Conjunct letters)
topics.whatToKnow: Letters with a small helper letter below (ಕ್ಕ, ಮ್ಮ, ಲ್ಲ, ಳ್ಳ). Child should read and write common ottakshara words like ಅಮ್ಮ, ಅಕ್ಕ, ಬೆಲ್ಲ, ಹಣ್ಣು.
topics.practiceAtHome: Write ಅಮ್ಮ, ಅಕ್ಕ, ಅಜ್ಜ, ಹಣ್ಣು, ಬೆಲ್ಲ on slips. Ask your child to read each and circle the ottakshara.

topics.name: ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರದ ವಿಧಗಳು (Types of conjuncts)
topics.whatToKnow: ಸಜಾತೀಯ ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರ — same letter doubles (ಕ್ಕ in ಅಕ್ಕ). ವಿಜಾತೀಯ ಒತ್ತಕ್ಷರ — two different letters join (ಸ್ತ in ಪುಸ್ತಕ).
topics.practiceAtHome: Give word pairs (ಅಕ್ಕ vs ಪುಸ್ತಕ) and ask: same-letter ottakshara or different-letter? Make it a sorting game.

topics.name: ಅಂಕಿಗಳು ಪದ ಸಹಿತ ೧-೯೦ (Numbers with words)
topics.whatToKnow: Read and write Kannada numerals ೧ to ೯೦ with their word forms (ಒಂದು, ಎರಡು, ಮೂರು...).
topics.practiceAtHome: Practice one decade a day (೧-೧೦, then ೧೧-೨೦...). Ask your child to write today's date in Kannada numerals!

topics.name: ಗುಣಿತಾಕ್ಷರಗಳು (Letter-vowel combinations)
topics.whatToKnow: Consonant + vowel forms: ಕ ಕಾ ಕಿ ಕೀ ಕು ಕೂ ಕೆ ಕೇ ಕೈ ಕೊ ಕೋ ಕೌ ಕಂ ಕಃ. Should be able to say and write for common letters.
topics.practiceAtHome: Chant the kagunita of one letter each day like a song. Then dictate 3 forms and let your child write them.

topics.name: ಪಾಠ ೧ - ಬಳ್ಳಿದ ಹಕ್ಕಿ (ಪದ್ಯ)
topics.whatToKnow: Recite the poem with correct pronunciation, know meanings of key words, and answer simple questions.
topics.practiceAtHome: Recite together twice daily — morning and bedtime. Ask what the poem is about in your child's own words.

subjects.subject: English
parentTips: Read one short English story or passage aloud daily — comprehension improves with listening + reading.
Turn grammar into games: 'spot the naming word' during dinner conversation.
For literature units, ask questions after reading: Who? What? Where? Why?
Practice writing 2-3 full sentences daily with capital letters and full stops.

topics.name: Section A: Reading Comprehension
topics.whatToKnow: Read a short unseen passage and answer simple questions from it. The answers are always inside the passage!
topics.practiceAtHome: Give a 4-5 line passage from any storybook. Ask 3 questions (who/what/where). Teach the trick: find the matching words in the passage to locate the answer.

topics.name: Grammar Unit 1: Naming Words (Nouns)
topics.whatToKnow: Naming words name a person (teacher), place (park), animal (dog) or thing (ball). From 'Why Flowers Are Colourful?'
topics.practiceAtHome: Play I-Spy with nouns: 'I spy a naming word in this room!' Ask your child to sort words into person/place/animal/thing columns.

topics.name: Grammar Unit 2: Words Used in Place of Naming Words (Pronouns)
topics.whatToKnow: He, She, It, They, We, I, You replace naming words. Example: 'Ravi is kind. HE helps everyone.' From 'Strange Friendship'.
topics.practiceAtHome: Say a sentence with a name and ask your child to repeat it using he/she/it: 'Mummy is cooking' → 'SHE is cooking.'

topics.name: Grammar Unit 3: Tenses (Yesterday And Today)
topics.whatToKnow: Action words change with time: Today I play → Yesterday I played. Now I am playing. Simple past vs present for common verbs.
topics.practiceAtHome: Every evening ask: 'What did you DO today?' — gently correct 'I goed' to 'I went'. Make pairs: play/played, jump/jumped, eat/ate, go/went.

topics.name: Literature Unit 1: My Pets
topics.whatToKnow: Read the lesson fluently, know word meanings, and answer textbook questions about the pets in the story.
topics.practiceAtHome: After reading, ask your child to describe their favourite pet from the lesson in 2 sentences.

topics.name: Literature Unit 2: My Trees Have No Leaves
topics.whatToKnow: Read fluently, understand the story/poem, know meanings of new words, answer simple questions.
topics.practiceAtHome: Discuss: why did the trees have no leaves? Relate it to trees your child sees outside — real connections stick!

quiz.q: Circle the naming word: 'The dog runs fast.'
Is 'school' a person, place, animal or thing?
